jobs.title: Director, Product Strategy & Roadmap
jobs.description:
Job Description

What's the opportunity?

We're looking for a product leader to own the roadmap for RBC's internal agentic AI platform end-to-end — from intake and prioritization through delivery and measurement. As Director, Product Strategy & Roadmap, you will decide what ships and when, ground those decisions in user value and adoption evidence, and own the product experience and analytics that make the platform usable and valuable at scale.

You will bring rigour to prioritization, fluency in agentic AI, and the credibility to partner with engineering on how the roadmap gets built — without owning the technical implementation.

Your responsibilities will include:

Roadmap ownership: Maintaining and communicating a rolling 12-month roadmap with clear, evidence-based prioritization rationale
Stakeholder intake: Capturing, assessing, and prioritizing feature requests from business lines, users, and leadership against a consistent value bar
User experience: Owning the end-to-end product experience across the platform — how users discover, adopt, build with, and get value from it — including the self-service builder, templates, and connector catalog as part of a coherent whole.
Product analytics: Building and maintaining adoption dashboards, usage telemetry, and value-realization measurement to drive decisions
Delivery partnership: Partnering with engineering on acceptance criteria, backlog, and delivery quality, staying engaged to protect the user outcome
Responsible AI in practice: Embedding the safety, governance, and transparency standards set by the AI Group's Safety and Responsible AI function into the roadmap and release gates
Market awareness: Conducting competitive and market analysis to inform platform direction

You're our ideal candidate if you:

Have 8+ years of product management experience, including 3+ in AI/ML products or enterprise platforms
Have a strong product-experience and design sensibility — able to shape how users discover, adopt, and succeed with a product, not only what features it has.
Have a deep working understanding of agentic AI: LLMs, tool-use, MCP connectors, RAG, and multi-agent orchestration
Have owned and delivered a product roadmap with measurable adoption outcomes
Are strongly analytical — able to define and track adoption metrics, build dashboards, and interpret telemetry
Have the technical fluency to partner with engineers on architecture decisions without writing code
Have agile delivery expertise: backlog grooming and acceptance-criteria definition
Have financial services awareness, or the ability to develop it quickly - understanding banking end-users (advisors, analysts, operations staff) and their workflow needs

Nice to have:

Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, HCI, or a related discipline
Product management certification (AIPM, Pragmatic Institute, CSPO, or SAFe)
Experience building developer platforms, APIs, or self-service builder tools
Familiarity with AI governance frameworks (NIST AI RMF, OSFI E-23, or equivalent)
Experience with prompt engineering, model evaluation, or fine-tuning in production
Background at a fintech, regtech, or major bank digital team

What's in it for you:

Drive AI transformation at one of Canada's largest and most respected financial institutions, with exposure to senior leadership across RBC
Be part of a newly formed, high-impact function within RBC's AI Group alongside experienced transformation leaders
A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock options where applicable
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact from a local-to-global scale

About the AI Group:

RBC's AI Group is the AI accelerator for RBC, with a focus on driving the shift from early-stage AI projects to scaled, client outcomes that amplify the impact of RBC's people. In addition to helping scale the biggest AI opportunities at RBC, the AI Group is responsible for advancing research into emerging use cases across generative and agentic AI, while maintaining expertise in security, responsible AI and regulatory expectations.

Inclusion and Equal Opportunity Employment:

RBC is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We are pleased to consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veterans status, Aboriginal/Native American status or any other legally-protected factors. Disability-related accommodations during the application process are available upon request.

jobs.description:
About Dialogue

Dialogue is the #1 virtual care provider in Canada. By developing our Integrated Health Platform🅫, we provide exceptional online health and wellness programs (primary care, mental health, iCBT, EAP, and wellness) to organizations that want to improve the wellness of their employees and families.

When It Comes To Our Work, We Set The Bar High. Together, We’re Transforming Health And Helping Millions Improve Their Well-being. We’re Firm Believers That Great People Don’t Settle On

Impact
Community
Growth
Excellence

Feel like you can make a difference? Good news, we saved you a seat!

Come as you are. As a proud equal-opportunity employer, Dialogue is dedicated to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace for everyone. Qualified applicants will be considered regardless of citizenship, ethnicity, race, colour, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability, age, or veteran status. Applicants who require specialized accommodation are encouraged to contact accessibility@dialogue.co .

AI Disclosure Statement

To ensure an efficient and fair review process, we utilize artificial intelligence tools to assist in the initial screening and assessment of applicants for this role.

⚠️ Recruitment Fraud Notice

Dialogue only contacts candidates through official @dialogue.co

email addresses. We never request payment, gift cards, or personal financial information at any stage of hiring, and we never extend an offer without a structured interview process. All open roles are listed exclusively at dialogue.co/en/careers

. If you receive a suspicious communication claiming to be from Dialogue, do not respond — report it to jobs@dialogue.co

and verify the role on our official careers page.

Your role as Director, Enterprise Account Management

Reporting to Melissa Trottier, Vice President, Customer Success, the Director, Enterprise Account Management has a mission to serve as a client advocate and trusted advisor for a highly strategic segment of Dialogue’s clientele, driving sustainable growth and ensuring long-term success.

This position requires an experienced leader, capable of managing strategic relationships, but above all, inspiring, mobilizing, and developing their team. The Director will play a key role in talent development, creating a collaborative environment, and achieving ambitious collective goals. They will be responsible for designing and implementing effective retention and engagement strategies, while ensuring our solutions optimally meet the complex and evolving needs of our clients. This leader brings a coaching and empowering management style that develops talent, fosters autonomy, and holds the team accountable to high standards.

The Director will be accountable for achieving a defined growth objective, ensuring the team generates sustainable and measurable value for both our clients and Dialogue. In close collaboration with the sales, partnerships, and marketing teams, this individual will act as the spokesperson for our most strategic clients, while strengthening team cohesion and performance to drive sustained growth.

What You'll Be Doing

Leading and growing a team of senior account managers, elevating their strategic advisor posture
Building and nurturing strategic relationships with key stakeholders, including C-suite and executive leaders
Supporting the team in designing value-based account strategies that drive retention, long-term expansion, and client advocacy, while identifying gaps and elevating the overall quality of execution
Representing Dialogue at industry events, conferences, and corporate functions to build lasting influence and credibility with HR market leaders, and bringing those insights back internally to inform our strategy
Influencing the strategic direction of our tech, clinical, and operational teams based on market signals, in order to evolve Dialogue's offering and stay anchored to real client needs
Acting as a central leader in aligning cross-functional teams to our clients’ complex needs, simplifying communication, and removing roadblocks

We'd love to hear from you if you have

5+ years of experience managing complex solutions with cross-functional teams
Proven experience negotiating and managing relationships with C-suite and senior executives, adopting a trusted advisor mindset
Excellent written and spoken communication skills in both French and English
Demonstrated ability to think strategically and critically, assessing opportunities and risks to develop relevant strategies
A track record of performance and success, showing a history of exceeding objectives
A strong bias for action and comfort with ambiguity
Mastery of a consultative account management approach: understanding the client’s business challenges before proposing a solution, and co-building value over time
Prior experience collaborating with a partner or broker network supporting shared clients, and understanding of tripartite relationships
Comfort with digital tools and a strong interest in technology and automation
Direct experience with human resources, employee benefits, the insurance industry, or corporate wellness programs is considered a strong asset

At Dialogue, your well-being is our priority

Benefits

Taking care of others also means taking care of our team! Depending on your role and employment status

, you could have access to the following benefits:

Access to the Dialogue app and virtual mental health support for you and your family
Fully funded insurance, a health spending account, dental coverage, and fitness reimbursement
4 weeks vacation, 9 wellness days, and 1 volunteer day
Hybrid work: 3 days/week in our Montreal or Toronto offices, excluding remote roles
Work abroad up to 4 weeks/year
Incentive plans, referral bonuses & RRSP matching
Learning via Coursera, external training budget & mentorship
Optional parental leave top-up

jobs.title: Director, Global Strategy - Enterprise Planning
jobs.description:
Your Opportunity at ARC’TERYX:

As the Director of Global Enterprise Planning on the Strategy team, you architect the planning system that connects Arc’teryx’s long-term strategy to annual priorities, resource allocation, and performance accountability. This is a systems-level role: you own the infrastructure that keeps leadership aligned, decisions grounded, and execution honest.

You own the enterprise planning process end-to-end – Strategic Planning Kickoff, Long-term Strategic Planning, AOP/budget prioritization, and Quarterly Business Reporting – while also owning the broader operating infrastructure: Excom and Board of Directors preparation, the strategic calendar, and the decision frameworks that ensure the right conversations happen with the right information at the right time.

You bring both architectural thinking and executional precision. You know when to build a new system and when to simplify an existing one. You are a credible executive partner, comfortable working directly with functional leaders and Finance to drive planning rigour across a complex, global business.

This role is based out of our North Vancouver office and is open to hybrid work (or remote Canada with travels to North Vancouver, BC). Candidates must be eligible to work in Canada.

Meet Your Future Team:

The Strategy team is a trusted partner to the executive leadership team in the development, prioritization, and oversight of our company strategies working cross-functionally across the business to ensure attainment of our long-term strategic objectives and goals. We provide strategic insights and frameworks to enable strategy development, cross-functional alignment and executive decision making. We are experts at translating complex, unstructured problems into clear executive level narrative and recommendations. Our team leads the company’s long-range strategic planning process, quarterly business reviews, and the development of an integrated performance management framework to connect our strategy to our annual operating budget and tactical operating plan.

If you were the Director, Global Strategy - Enterprise Planning here are some of the core activities you would be doing:

Owning the design, governance, and continuous evolution of the enterprise planning system, ensuring strategic planning, annual operating planning, resource allocation, and performance reporting operate as an integrated enterprise process

Leading the execution of the enterprise planning cycle, including Strategic Planning Kickoff, Long-Term Strategic Planning, and Quarterly Business Reviews, and partnering with Finance on Annual Operating Plan (AOP) and budget prioritization connected to business strategy

Establishing and governing the enterprise planning cadence, ensuring cross-functional alignment, decision readiness, and the timely progression of key strategic milestones

Building and maintaining the decision frameworks, governance structures, and planning standards that support enterprise-wide prioritization, accountability, and effective decision-making

Partnering closely with Finance and business leaders to translate strategic priorities into actionable plans, resource allocation decisions, and measurable outcomes

Leading the planning and coordination of Executive Committee and Board reviews, ensuring strategic issues are clearly framed, decisions are supported by relevant insights, and resulting actions are effectively tracked

Managing the enterprise portfolio of strategic initiatives, tracking progress, interdependencies, risks, and outcomes while escalating issues requiring executive attention

Developing scenarios, business cases, and trade-off analyses that enable leaders to evaluate opportunities, risks, investments, and resource allocation decisions

Providing fact-based analysis, insights, and recommendations to support executive decision-making, prioritization, and enterprise performance discussions

Establishing enterprise performance management frameworks, scorecards, KPIs, and reporting mechanisms that drive accountability, transparency, and execution against strategic objectives

Driving alignment across executive leadership, functions, regions, Finance, and Amer Sports to establish a consistent enterprise planning and performance management operating model

Maintaining visibility to key strategic and execution risks, ensuring mitigation plans are developed, monitored, and integrated into enterprise planning processes

Developing executive-level communications, planning documents, and leadership briefings that translate complex business information into clear priorities, recommendations, and actions

Serving as the steward of enterprise planning effectiveness, continuously evaluating planning processes, governance, and reporting mechanisms to improve decision quality, organizational alignment, and business outcomes

Developing and maintaining the tools, templates, governance processes, and planning methodologies that strengthen enterprise planning capability and support execution against strategic and business plans

Here are some of the things you could be working on in the future:

Evolving the enterprise planning system as the business scales—adding new planning horizons, integrating regional complexity, and improving the speed and quality of decisions

Building repeatable frameworks and playbooks for planning processes that reduce dependency on heroic individual effort and increase organizational capability

Partnering with Finance and regional teams to develop integrated financial and strategic planning models that connect long-range ambition to annual resource reality

Developing the next generation of performance management tools—moving from tracking to accountability, and from reporting to action

Supporting the Strategy team’s broader operating model evolution as new capability areas come online

Are you our next Director, Global Strategy - Enterprise Planning?

You have a bachelor’s degree in business, strategy, or related field

You have 10+ years of professional work experience in strategic planning, management consulting, project management, consumer products and/or retail

You have a demonstrated track record as an outstanding problem solver and strategic You think in systems – you can see how the strategic planning connects to the budget planning, how the QBR connects to accountability, and how the strategic calendar creates or destroys leadership bandwidth

You are a credible executive partner with the communication skills to work directly with a CDR and functional leaders, and to translate complexity into decisions

You have significant experience partnering with Finance on resource allocation, budget prioritization, and performance tracking

You bring sharp analytical capability and strong written communication, and you can build a rigorous framework and write a clear executive brief

You have experience working across regional and global operating models, ideally with exposure to retail or consumer-facing businesses

You are organized without being rigid, and you know when the plan needs to change and how to move the system accordingly

You demonstrate high emotional intelligence, sound judgment, and the ability to influence without authority across senior stakeholders

You hold yourself and others to a high standard for quality of thinking, clarity of communication, and follow-through

Compensation:
The salary range for this role is CAD$149,000 - CAD$195,000 

Total Rewards

Most new team members join between the start and midpoint of the range, where you can contribute right away while continuing to grow your craft, your collaborations, and your impact at Arc’teryx. This range reflects market alignment and the scope of the role. Individual pay is determined by your skills, experience, and level of responsibility.

We’re committed to fair, equitable, and competitive pay, reviewed regularly to ensure internal alignment and market relevance. Transparency is part of how we follow through on our commitments and how we honour the value you bring to our team.

In addition to base pay, Arc’teryx supports people through benefits designed to sustain both work and life:

Health & wellbeing
- Extended health, dental, and vision coverage, including mental health support, fertility benefits, gender-affirming care and a 24/7 Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

Financial wellbeing
- RRSP matching and eligibility for Arc'teryx Annual Incentive Plan and access to Employee Stock Purchase program (ESPP) where applicable.

Time & Flexibilit
y - Paid time off, wellness time, and No Wasted Day program (dedicated paid days to get outside & explore).

Family support
- Parental leave top-up and a nesting period for new parents.

Growth, community & gear
- Professional development opportunities, Arc'teryx Academies (outdoor skill-building events) , Employee Belonging Councils, and access to employee discounts and Pro Deals (exclusive discounted pricing on gear).
  *Eligibility for certain programs may vary by role.

Your role as Director, Enterprise Account Management

Reporting to Melissa Trottier, Vice President, Customer Success, the Director, Enterprise Account Management has a mission to serve as a client advocate and trusted advisor for a highly strategic segment of Dialogue’s clientele, driving sustainable growth and ensuring long-term success.

This position requires an experienced leader, capable of managing strategic relationships, but above all, inspiring, mobilizing, and developing their team. The Director will play a key role in talent development, creating a collaborative environment, and achieving ambitious collective goals. They will be responsible for designing and implementing effective retention and engagement strategies, while ensuring our solutions optimally meet the complex and evolving needs of our clients. This leader brings a coaching and empowering management style that develops talent, fosters autonomy, and holds the team accountable to high standards.

The Director will be accountable for achieving a defined growth objective, ensuring the team generates sustainable and measurable value for both our clients and Dialogue. In close collaboration with the sales, partnerships, and marketing teams, this individual will act as the spokesperson for our most strategic clients, while strengthening team cohesion and performance to drive sustained growth.

What You'll Be Doing

Leading and growing a team of senior account managers, elevating their strategic advisor posture
Building and nurturing strategic relationships with key stakeholders, including C-suite and executive leaders
Supporting the team in designing value-based account strategies that drive retention, long-term expansion, and client advocacy, while identifying gaps and elevating the overall quality of execution
Representing Dialogue at industry events, conferences, and corporate functions to build lasting influence and credibility with HR market leaders, and bringing those insights back internally to inform our strategy
Influencing the strategic direction of our tech, clinical, and operational teams based on market signals, in order to evolve Dialogue's offering and stay anchored to real client needs
Acting as a central leader in aligning cross-functional teams to our clients’ complex needs, simplifying communication, and removing roadblocks

We'd love to hear from you if you have

5+ years of experience managing complex solutions with cross-functional teams
Proven experience negotiating and managing relationships with C-suite and senior executives, adopting a trusted advisor mindset
Excellent written and spoken communication skills in both French and English
Demonstrated ability to think strategically and critically, assessing opportunities and risks to develop relevant strategies
A track record of performance and success, showing a history of exceeding objectives
A strong bias for action and comfort with ambiguity
Mastery of a consultative account management approach: understanding the client’s business challenges before proposing a solution, and co-building value over time
Prior experience collaborating with a partner or broker network supporting shared clients, and understanding of tripartite relationships
Comfort with digital tools and a strong interest in technology and automation
Direct experience with human resources, employee benefits, the insurance industry, or corporate wellness programs is considered a strong asset

At Dialogue, your well-being is our priority

Benefits

, you could have access to the following benefits:

Access to the Dialogue app and virtual mental health support for you and your family

Hybrid work: 3 days/week in our Montreal or Toronto offices, excluding remote roles

Optional parental leave top-up

Department Overview

The Planning and Management Control department produces comprehensive reports for senior management, delivers monthly financial performance commentary, and coordinates annual budgets. The team controls regional expenses, manages expense allocations, handles forecasting, and processes monthly closing entries for financing activities. It also serves as the primary interface between business lines, support functions, and Finance on finance-related matters.

Primary Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Reporting

Coordinate monthly close meetings and oversee monthly P&L forecasts supporting asset and liability management and hedging activities.
Manage quarterly forecasts and other forecasting requirements.
Coordinate and deliver the annual regional budget process.
Ensure accurate monthly financial data production within established reporting deadlines.

Management Reporting & Analysis

Prepare monthly and quarterly dashboards for management committees, board meetings, and regulatory bodies.
Review and publish the team’s monthly P&L analysis.
Respond to inquiries from senior Finance leadership and executive stakeholders.

Operational Management

Ensure appropriate monthly bonus accruals.
Process monthly closing entries for financing activities.
Serve as a key Finance contact for management.
Prepare monthly intercompany recharges and semi-annual billing, responding to related inquiries as needed.

Team Leadership

Manage and develop a team of nine professionals across multiple locations.
Delegate effectively and encourage collaboration across teams and functions.

Key Internal Contacts

Regional CFO.
Central management reporting teams.
Management committee members.
Other Finance teams.
IT, HR, and Risk departments.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree required.
Approximately 10–15 years of relevant professional experience.

Technical Competencies

Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.
Expertise in Essbase.
Strong understanding of organizational structures within a complex financial institution.
Strong knowledge of accounting principles and standards, including GAAP and IFRS.
Expertise in management control principles, standards, and processes.

Essential Skills

Analytical & Decision-Making

Strong ability to analyze and summarize complex information.
Effective prioritization and ability to work independently.
Strong decision-making and problem-solving skills.

Leadership & Collaboration

Proven ability to work effectively in a team environment.
Strong delegation and collaboration skills across functions.
Ability to develop team members.

Adaptability

Flexibility to adapt to changing business environments.
Ability to lead departmental transformation projects involving IT tools and reporting support.
Ability to organize activities across multiple locations, including establishing policies, procedures, and responsibilities.

new_jobs.description:
SETUP
: Mostly remote, only required 1-2 times/month in office. Located in North York, ON

CONTRACT
: 18 months

About the Opportunity

Financial Reporting & Consolidations:
Lead the preparation and review of monthly, quarterly, and annual consolidated financial statements and management reporting.
Oversee the consolidation of multiple legal entities/business units, including intercompany balances, eliminations, foreign currency translation, and consolidation adjustments.
Ensure financial reporting is accurate, complete, appropriately supported, and delivered within established reporting timelines.
Maintain and enhance consolidation processes, reporting packages, and financial controls.
Partner with business units and finance teams to resolve consolidation and reporting issues.

US GAAP & IFRS:
Serve as a key technical accounting resource for matters involving US GAAP and IFRS.
Research and assess complex accounting issues and provide recommendations regarding appropriate accounting treatment.
Monitor new and emerging accounting standards and assess their impact on the organization.
Lead the implementation of new accounting standards and changes to existing reporting requirements.
Prepare and review technical accounting memos, position papers, and supporting documentation.
Support accounting matters involving areas such as revenue recognition, leases, business combinations, foreign currency, impairment, and other complex transactions, as applicable.

Controls, Audit & Compliance:
Maintain a strong financial control environment across the reporting and consolidation processes.
Coordinate with internal and external auditors and support quarterly and annual audit requirements.
Ensure appropriate documentation and supporting schedules are maintained for significant accounting judgments, estimates, and transactions.
Identify reporting and control risks and implement process improvements to strengthen financial governance.
Leadership & Business Partnership:
Lead, coach, and develop a team of 4–5 finance and accounting professionals, establishing clear responsibilities and development priorities.
Provide technical guidance and oversight to the team while promoting accountability and high-quality execution.
Partner closely with FP&A, Corporate Accounting, Tax, Treasury, and other finance functions to ensure consistency and accuracy across financial reporting.
Work with senior leadership to communicate financial reporting matters, accounting implications, and significant issues.
Support acquisitions, integrations, restructuring activities, and other strategic initiatives from an accounting and reporting perspective.

Process Improvement:
Drive improvements to the financial close, consolidation, and reporting processes with a focus on accuracy, efficiency, standardization, and scalability.
Identify opportunities to automate manual reporting and reconciliation activities.
Strengthen reporting processes, systems, and controls as the organization grows and reporting requirements evolve.

About You

CPA designation.
10+ years of progressive accounting and financial reporting experience, including significant experience in a leadership capacity.
Strong technical knowledge and practical application of US GAAP and/or IFRS.
Significant experience with multi-entity consolidations, including intercompany eliminations and foreign currency considerations.
Experience leading and developing accounting or financial reporting teams.
